html:
The Mbeiwum were an Aboriginal Australian people of the western Cape York Peninsula in north Queensland. The map shows them only in 1783 and 1800.

Almost nothing is recorded of them beyond their name and a small territory on the Gulf side of the peninsula. They lived among many small neighbouring peoples, including the Awngthim, the Lotiga and the Wik, each with its own speech. Missions and the bauxite mining town of Weipa later changed this coast. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
